title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 45-46
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 45 to 46 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'ऋतुः सुदर्शनः कालः परमेष्ठी परिग्रहः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 45 to 46 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 45 to 46.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 45 to 46** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **ऋतुः सुदर्शनः कालः परमेष्ठी परिग्रहः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**ऋतुः सुदर्शनः कालः परमेष्ठी परिग्रहः । उग्रः संवत्सरो दक्षो विश्रामो विश्वदक्षिणः ॥** **विस्तारः स्थावरस्थाणुः प्रमाणं बीजमव्ययम् । अर्थोऽनर्थो महाकोशो महाभोगो महाधनः ॥**

He is the sacrifice itself and the wheel Sudarshana. Time, the Supreme One who embraces all, is that God of gods. Fierce, the year, skilful, the place of rest, the offering of the universe. He is the vast expanse, both the moving and the unmoving. The proof of truth and the seed that never fails is that God of gods. Meaning and loss, a great treasury, great enjoyment and great wealth.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 45 to 46 mean?
faq.a: He is the sacrifice itself and the wheel Sudarshana. Time, the Supreme One who embraces all, is that God of gods. Fierce, the year, skilful, the place of rest, the offering of the universe. He is the vast expanse, both the moving and the unmoving. The proof of truth and the seed that never fails is that God of gods. Meaning and loss, a great treasury, great enjoyment and great wealth.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
